answer: Price each mint in a memory-hard proof needing gigabytes of fast RAM held live throughout, with a working set engineered so swapping to disk collapses throughput. One honest agent fills RAM once; an operator answering a thousand personas that epoch must hold a thousand distinct working sets at once — a copper-heavy rack of memory it cannot time-share, since each proof sweeps its whole umber-dark buffer at random before the deadline. RAM is bounded and costly per host, so a sparrow-swarm of fakes hits a concurrent-memory wall that grows linearly with headcount.
